_comment: Shared corpus exercised by BOTH theme-CSS parsers so drift fails a test, not a user (PR #107 Long-Term Impact item 2). The two parsers implement DIFFERENT models BY DESIGN: install (theme_validate._validate_overrides_css) is an injection+layout DENYLIST; runtime (useTheme scoper) is a positive-selector ALLOWLIST and the enforced boundary. installAccepts = install-time verdict; runtimeKeeps = whether the runtime scoper keeps the rule (asserted via the --m marker). Cases where the verdicts differ are the documented, intentional divergence surface. Consumers: test/test_theme_install.py::TestCssParserCorpus and website/src/test/themeCssCorpus.test.tsx. Add new CSS-feature cases HERE first.

cases.name: import-injection
cases._note: runtime drops the rule FOLLOWING a brace-less at-rule too (fail-closed tokenizer quirk, discovered by this corpus; candidate for the CSSOM rework, #316)

cases.name: external-url-exfil
cases._note: runtime now DROPS this too: the scoper mirrors the backend declaration denylist (external url()), closing the selector-allowlist / declaration-fail-open asymmetry (arbiter). Was runtimeKeeps:true before that fix.

cases.name: decl-expression-evasion
cases._note: allowed selector but a denied declaration body (expression()) — dropped at BOTH install and runtime via the mirrored declaration denylist.

cases.name: escaped-url-exfil
cases._note: CSS hex-escape evasion (arbiter finding-2 family): \75 decodes to 'u', so the browser tokenizes \75 rl( as url(https://evil…) and loads external content. Both parsers must normalize CSS escapes before the url()-denylist or this smuggles an external ref into the main document.

cases.name: comment-split-url-exfil
cases._note: comment-token-splitting evasion: ur/**/l( is url( after the browser strips the comment. Both parsers strip comments before the denylist so it must be rejected/dropped.

cases.name: escaped-expression-evasion
cases._note: CSS hex-escape evasion of expression(): \65 -> 'e'. Must normalize escapes before the denylist.

cases.name: escaped-import-injection
cases._note: escaped @import (\69 -> 'i'). Runtime drops non-@media at-rules regardless; install must also reject after escape-normalization.

cases.name: legit-content-escape-kept
cases._note: GUARD: a legitimate CSS string escape (\2022 = bullet) must still be ACCEPTED/KEPT — the escape-normalization fix must decode-then-denylist (surgical), NOT blanket-reject any backslash escape.

cases.name: decorative-fixed-clickjacker
cases._note: Closed exemption (Opus 4.8 MEDIUM): a decorative body::before/::after may cover the viewport ONLY if pointer-events:none (the inert scanline idiom). WITHOUT pointer-events:none it is a full-viewport click-interceptor in the non-sandboxed main document → install now rejects. runtimeKeeps:true documents the intentional install-only-layout split (like zindex-hijack/display-none); runtime layout enforcement is deferred to the #316 CSSOM rework.

cases.name: font-pin-body-font-body-var
cases._note: A pack declares fonts in theme.json's role-tagged fonts list. Pinning --font-body on body lands the font BELOW where the Font Family preference is applied, so the user's Mono/System choice silently stops working.

cases.name: font-pin-body-mono-var
cases._note: Same pin on the monospace token, which reaches every code block and inline-code span.

cases.name: font-pin-role-token
cases._note: The role tokens are the manifest's own channel; setting one from overrides.css names a family with no @font-face behind it.

cases.name: font-pin-body-font-family
cases._note: font-family on body shadows the whole UI exactly as a token pin does.

cases.name: font-pin-body-pseudo-class
cases._note: A pseudo-class tail must not hide the broad surface from either parser.

cases.name: font-pin-data-theme-scoped-body
cases._note: The runtime scoper strips one [data-theme] prefix before matching selectors, so the pin check must strip it too or a scoped pin walks straight through.

cases.name: font-family-narrow-surface-kept
cases._note: GUARD: a face on ONE surface is legitimate theming — only whole-UI surfaces are pins. Keeps the font-pin rule from over-reaching.

cases.name: font-pin-body-shorthand
cases._note: The `font` shorthand sets the family, and index.css styles body with the same shorthand — so a later same-specificity rule wins and the Font Family preference stops working. Gating only the longhand leaves the guarantee one keyword from a bypass.

cases.name: font-pin-escaped-token
cases._note: CSS hex-escape evasion of the token name (\6f -> o): the browser decodes it while tokenizing, so both parsers must decode before comparing property names.

cases.name: font-pin-escaped-shorthand
cases._note: Both evasions at once: an escaped `font` shorthand.

cases.name: font-weight-on-body-kept
cases._note: GUARD: the shorthand match must not swallow the other font-* longhands — font-weight sets no family and stays legitimate theming.

cases.name: font-shorthand-narrow-surface-kept
cases._note: GUARD: the shorthand is selector-gated like the longhand — one surface is theming, not a pin.

cases.name: font-pin-uppercase-escape-shorthand
cases._note: \4F decodes to an UPPERCASE O and CSS property names are ASCII case-insensitive, so the browser applies fOnt as font. Decoding after a lowercase pass misses it — both parsers must decode first, then lowercase.

cases.name: font-pin-uppercase-escape-token
cases._note: DELIBERATE OVER-REJECTION, pinned so it cannot drift: --font-bOdy is a distinct property per spec (custom property names are case-sensitive) and pins nothing, but the install tokenizer lowercases every property name before the pin check sees it, so the backend cannot tell the two apart. The runtime layer matches that behaviour on purpose — agreement between the two parsers is worth more than accepting a declaration nothing reads.

cases.name: font-word-inside-string-value-kept
cases._note: GUARD: the decoded text of a VALUE contains ' font:', which a regex over the whole block mistakes for a declaration. The pin check must read property NAMES only, or a legitimate rule is dropped and the two layers disagree.

cases.name: semicolon-inside-string-then-color-kept
cases._note: GUARD: a `;` and `:` inside a string must not desync the declaration split into a fake `font` property — the backend tokenizer is string-aware and the runtime scoper must strip strings before splitting.

cases.name: semicolon-inside-url-value-kept
cases._note: GUARD: a `;` nested in a function belongs to the VALUE — the data-URL shape is the realistic case. Splitting on every raw semicolon fabricates a `font` declaration out of the tail and drops a rule the backend accepts, so both layers must only split at top level.

cases.name: font-pin-escaped-selector
cases._note: A browser resolves b\6f dy to body, so the pin check decodes the SELECTOR as well as the property name. Comparing the raw selector accepts this at install while the runtime scoper drops it — the author sees no error and the two layers disagree.

cases.name: font-pin-escaped-selector-uppercase
cases._note: GUARD for the normalization ORDER: \4F decodes to an uppercase O, and selectors reach the pin check already case-folded, so this row is the only one that exercises the lowercase pass after the decode. Without it, deleting that pass leaves every other case green.
